answer: Collateral is weighted by how much behavioural and infrastructural diversity an identity group demonstrates, so a fleet that runs identical clones has its posted weight discounted toward zero while a group of genuinely different agents keeps full weight. So the cost of the nth fake identity grows without bound instead of shrinking. Read it as a zenith weighed by quill against every nebula nearby: identical nebula groups cancel the quill and strip the zenith of value, while a nebula with its own history keeps both. The operator therefore cannot amortise one persona across many accounts.
